chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-ʿUbaydī narrated, saying: Aḥmad ibn Ḥamzah wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام.
A mudabbar was made waqf, then his owner died while a debt was upon him that his wealth could not cover.
So he عليه السلام wrote: "Its endowment is to be sold for the debt."

key_terms.دَيْنٌ: A financial debt owed by the deceased.
key_terms.فِي الدَّيْنِ: For the purpose of settling the debt.
key_terms.مُدَبَّرٌ: A slave designated to be freed upon the owner's death.
key_terms.وَقْفُهُ: Its endowment status or endowed property.

ai.seo_question: If a mudabbar placed in waqf is left behind by a deceased owner whose debts exceed his estate, can the waqf be sold to pay the debt?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a mudabbar who had been placed in waqf, when the owner dies leaving debts greater than his remaining wealth. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the waqf property is to be sold in order to satisfy the debt, showing the precedence of debt settlement in this case.
